item.title: Wide Angle X-Ray Scattering Data Set of Gypsum Compounds
item.description:
Markus Wilhelm, Frank Lotter, Bastian Engelmann
Scientific Data, vol. 13, issue 1
DOI: 10.1038/s41597-026-08677-z
Abstract This Data Descriptor presents a comprehensive dataset focused on the qualitative and quantitative detection of impurities in recycled gypsum using Wide-Angle X-Ray Scattering (WAXS). Generated within the GIPScycle research project, the dataset aims to address the challenge of identifying mineral fibres (e.g., asbestos) and other contaminants in gypsum waste streams. It comprises 1,920 WAXS diffractograms derived from defined reference materials, artificially created mixtures with varying contaminant concentrations (ranging from 0.001 wt% to > 1 wt%), and real-world recycling batches. The data captures structural properties and crystalline phases, providing a robust basis for training machine learning models for automated quality control. The dataset supports the development of detection methods capable of identifying mineral fibres below the regulatory threshold of 0.1 wt%.

item.title: A Multimodal Dataset of 18th-Century Prints for Segmentation and Analysis of Rocaille Ornaments
item.description:
Thomas Hudcovic, Ines Röckl, Julian Jachmann, Gabriel Zachmann
Scientific Data, vol. 13, issue 1
DOI: 10.1038/s41597-026-08703-0
Abstract We present a multimodal dataset for the computational study of 18th-century Rococo ornamental prints. Rocaille, a characteristic ornament of the period, exhibits a continuously transforming morphology that has historically resisted systematic formal description. The dataset comprises 1,611 high-resolution digitizations from major German collections, accompanied by expert-curated bilingual metadata and commentary describing iconography and ornamental morphology. A subset of 229 images includes pixel-accurate segmentation masks distinguishing the structural volutes and comb-like extensions of the Rocaille. The images, structured metadata, textual descriptions, and segmentation annotations together support computational analyses ranging from visual multimodal retrieval and semantic segmentation to morphological analysis. As technical validation, we train two standard vision backbones for segmentation, showing that the annotations provide a learnable segmentation signal and that pre-training on both external data and our dataset can support downstream learning. Code, data splits, trained model weights, and evaluation outputs are provided to facilitate reproducible use of the resource. The dataset provides a foundation for cross-disciplinary research at the intersection of art history, digital humanities, and computer vision.
